title: The Simplest Math Problem No One Can Solve - Collatz Conjecture
beats: Most dangerous problem in math; Erdos says math is not ripe for it
Pick 7, apply odd 3n+1 / even halve, narrate every step to 1 and the 4-2-1 loop
State the conjecture; list its many names
Mathematicians say working on it is infamous; warned off by senior colleagues
Hailstones: numbers as altitude; 26 vs 27 (111 steps, peak 9232 above Everest)
Kontorovich and Sinai look for patterns in the paths
Log of path looks like stock market; coin-flip random walk with downward trend
Leading-digit histogram built sequence by sequence; Benford's law emerges
Benford's law cannot answer the loop question
Naive view: odd triples, even halves, so should grow; actually 3/2 then divide by 2^k gives 3/4 average shrink
Directed graph as streams into a river; rotated coral version
Two ways to be false: divergent seed or other loop
Checked up to 2^68, loop must be >186 billion long; likely true but not proof
Scatterplot strategy: show each sequence dips below its seed
Terras 1976, 1979, 1994 improvements; Tao 2019 almost all numbers
Everyone seeks proofs, nobody searches counterexamples; mathematician's own story
Almost all vs all: perfect squares fraction shrinks yet infinite
Turing machine tape: 68 squares tested; finite behavior can be arbitrarily engineered
Conway's FRACTRAN, halting problem, maybe undecidable
Humility reflections; numbers peculiar; return to Erdos quote

metrics.examples: 7, 26, 27, 341, big random seed, 9663; then squares and Polya as counter-analogies; grow from tiny hand case to astronomical scale
metrics.ending: Callback to Erdos quote, humility, then sponsor

new_moves.what: Experts say do not work on this, building stakes and mystery before any content

new_moves.name: evidence-undercut
new_moves.what: Present impressive evidence (2^68), then show why it is weak via analogies (squares, Polya)

new_moves.what: Frame a conjecture by enumerating how it could fail

theory: The video teaches by running the dumbest possible procedure by hand until the learner owns it, then repeatedly raising the scale and undercutting each comfortable conclusion. The strongest transferable move is pairing evidence with its limits (brute force to 2^68, then Polya at 10^361), which teaches how to judge proof rather than just facts.
velocity: Scene builder: hand-run iteration with a stepping animation, then batch run of thousands with a live histogram
Orchestrator: after any evidence beat, schedule a 'why is this not proof' beat
Learner model: ask the learner to predict grow vs shrink before revealing the 3/4 average (misconception probe)
Evals: check tutor states limits of evidence, not just results
quote: Mathematics is not yet ripe enough for such questions
